calls.head: Pittsburgh gets to the dangerous areas
calls.body: Pittsburgh ranks 5th of 32 for shot quality (one expected goal for every 15.0 unblocked shots); Washington ranks 23rd for keeping shots to the outside.
calls.call: Pittsburgh needs no more than its usual 15.0 unblocked shots per expected goal.
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 3 and 2 games this season
calls.happened: Pittsburgh needed 11.2 unblocked shots per expected goal, against its usual 15.0.

calls.head: Expect Pittsburgh to fire from everywhere
calls.body: Pittsburgh ranks 8th of 32 for shot volume (60.2 shot attempts per 60 at 5-on-5); Washington ranks 24th for shot suppression.
calls.call: Pittsburgh takes at least its usual 60.2 shot attempts per 60 at 5-on-5.
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 3 and 2 games this season
calls.happened: Pittsburgh took 59.0 shot attempts per 60 at 5-on-5 (adjusted for score and venue), against its usual 60.2.

calls.head: Two of the league’s busiest games meet
calls.body: Pittsburgh’s games average 84.2 unblocked shots per 60 at 5-on-5, both teams combined (6th of 32 for pace); Washington’s average 83.3 (9th).
calls.call: The game runs at more than the two teams’ usual 83.8 unblocked shots per 60 at 5-on-5.
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 3 and 2 games this season
calls.happened: The game ran at 88.7 unblocked shots per 60 at 5-on-5, both teams combined, against the two teams’ usual 83.8 and a league average of 81.8.

WSH.head: We had this close to even (46% for Washington), and Washington came through.

PIT.head: We had this close to even (54% for Pittsburgh), and it went Washington’s way.

surprises.head: Pittsburgh got to the dangerous areas
surprises.body: Pittsburgh needed 11.2 unblocked shots per expected goal at 5-on-5, against its usual 15.0 and a league average of 15.8. Over the last three seasons, a team strayed this far about once every 20 games.

surprises.head: Pittsburgh hardly hit anyone
surprises.body: Pittsburgh’s hit score in the close stretches of the game was 31, against its usual 72 (100 is league average, adjusted for the arena’s scorer). Over the last three seasons, a team strayed this far about once every 10 games.
